subject: Sizing follow-up: Surfside Labs deployment mode and TPS profile
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@surfside.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Green <natalie@surfside.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T14:02:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Hi Marissa / Ben —

Really appreciate the demo today; the low-latency routing and the cost controls looked promising. Per our internal discussion we want to double-check the deployment options before we proceed to procurement: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC. Two things we need clarified to move forward: 1) if we pick Dedicated, what GPU families make sense for our load (we're evaluating A100 vs H100) and 2) an estimate of required concurrency/TPS so we can budget the committed capacity.

Attached is a small sample of our token distribution and a weekly TPS curve (rough). Key notes:
- Peak TPS target: ~650 requests/sec (mix of short chat and longer generation)
- 95% of calls are ~120 tokens in / 150 tokens out average
- ~18% of requests are longer (>800 tokens) and can tolerate slightly higher latency

Can you confirm whether Dedicated would be the right path for predictable latency and also what a ballpark GPU sizing would look like? If Hosted is viable, what tradeoffs on cost and throttling should we expect?

Thanks,
Samir
VP of Product
Surfside Labs

(attachment: surfside-prod-token-sample.csv, surfside_traffic_curve.png)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@surfside.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-04T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the quick summary and for attaching the token/sample curves — super helpful. Short answers up front:
- Dedicated is likely the best fit for predictable p95 latency and capacity isolation at your scale, especially given the sustained 650 TPS peak and the tail of long responses.
- H100-class instances give better headroom for long-sequence tails and lower p95 for mixed-length traffic; A100 can be more cost-efficient for primarily short sequences but will need more GPUs to cover the long-request percent.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) Ben and I will run a quick sizing calc against your CSV and return a 2-option proposal (H100-focused and A100-focused) with estimated pool size, expected p50/p95 latency, and a committed capacity quote.
2) We'll include a Hosted-vs-Dedicated appendix that outlines expected throttling behavior and burst/fallback policies if you prefer Hosted initially.
3) If you want Private VPC, we can include a checklist and an estimated effort (networking, KMS) — usually a +4 week lead.

Ben, Karthik — can you take the attached token CSV and the TPS curve and do a fast back-of-envelope sizing? Aim for two configurations: one optimized for cost (A100 mix) and one optimized for latency/tail (H100 mix). Include recommended concurrency per model replica, estimated GPUs, and expected p95 for the median token profile.

Samir / Natalie — we'll share the sizing spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow and propose a follow-up slot Thurs or Fri to walk through the tradeoffs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
(attachment: redwood_dedicated_quote_v1.pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-05T10:15:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Samir's sample and Marissa's notes. Quick notes from my side after a first pass on the CSV:
- Baseline assumption: medium-sized LLM (13b-34b) with kv-cache friendly serving; token mix from Samir suggests ~75% of calls are sub-200 tokens which is good for batching.
- For 650 TPS peak:
  * A100 option (cost-optimized): roughly 12-16 A100 GPUs with batching and burst slots. Expect p95 ~220-320ms for short calls, but long tails (~800+ tokens) will push p95 higher occasionally.
  * H100 option (latency-optimized): roughly 8-10 H100 GPUs with similar batching; p95 ~120-190ms for majority of calls and far more consistent under mixed-length load.
- Concurrency: recommend per-replica concurrency of 4 for H100, 6-8 for A100 depending on model quantization. We'll include quantization notes in the sheet.
- Caching: prefix caching could reduce cost by ~12% for your workload (many repeated prompts).

Karthik — can you run a small expected-latency calc assuming: 650 TPS peak, token avg in/out 270, longest 2% at 1k tokens. Include expected token-s/sec per GPU for the two GPU families and the recommended replica concurrency.

I can assemble the two-option spreadsheet and a short appendix on Hosted tradeoffs (rate limits, no dedicated SLA, lower predictability on p95).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@surfside.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Green <natalie@surfside.ai>
Date: 2027-08-06T18:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Hi Samir / Natalie —

Thanks for the sample and patience. Attached is a short sizing summary (I'll drop the full spreadsheet to the Drive link). Highlights:
- H100 configuration recommendation: 9 H100 GPUs, per-replica concurrency 4, expected sustained p95 ~160ms for the median profile, handles 650 TPS peak with autoscale headroom for 20% burst.
- A100 configuration recommendation: 14 A100 GPUs, per-replica concurrency 6, expected sustained p95 ~280ms for median short calls, can be ~450-700ms on 800+ token tails unless you add KV-prefetch or more GPUs.
- Cost delta: H100 committed pool ~ +27% monthly vs the A100 configuration, but provides better p95 and fewer GPUs to manage. We included a sensitivity for token growth +30% and for off-hours load.
- Hosted path (if you prefer to start there): feasible for evaluation but not recommended for predictable SLAs at this volume — we'd expect occasional throttling under regional capacity pressure; dedicated gives SLA and isolated throughput.

Next steps:
1) We'll place the two-option sizing sheet in the Drive (link above) and the PDF quote is attached.
2) If you confirm H100 or A100 preference, we'll draft a Mutual Action Plan for procurement and a 4-week schedule for Dedicated onboarding (network, customer config, monitoring, runbook).

Would you prefer a 30-min follow-up tomorrow to go line-by-line on the tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
